sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Accredited US bachelor’s degree or equivalent, adequate mathematical preparation and normally GPA at least
3.0 in upper-division and any graduate work. Below-minimum applicants may apply with an explanatory letter.
UChicago math bachelor is an eligible degree route if completed in time; GPA/history remain unverified. Only
fall PhD admission; mathematics master’s is actuarial only. [s4] [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply early enough for multi-step processing: initial form takes 2-3 business days to load; then pay fee and
complete MyStatus documents. Transcript verification takes another 2-3 business days. Use assigned UT EID,
never create a duplicate. Choose primary interest ANG for algebra/number theory/geometry, optional
secondary and up to three specific areas; choices guide reviewers but do not bind your eventual specialty. [s2]
[s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
List faculty of interest in SOP; no prior supervisor approval requirement appears in math instructions. For
academic admissions questions, Graduate Advisor Tim Perutz: gradadv@math.utexas.edu; program
administrator Robyn Lynch: robyn.lynch@austin.utexas.edu. Individual faculty availability remains to be
confirmed. [s1] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Initial Slate form followed by MyStatus/EID email, fee payment and verified documents. Central processing
estimate2-3business days is more conservative than math24-48hours. Monitor MyStatus; upload scans of
official transcripts, not unofficial placeholders. Referee reminders/updates supported. For international
insurance, benefits-eligible appointment waiver must be processed by 10thclass day5p.m. fall/spring
or1stclass day5p.m. summer; exact Fall2027date not yet published. [s2] [s12]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Explicit Fall 2027 application opening and August 2026 GRE update. Deadline year inferred from current
cycle’s December 15; precise time unknown. Pay scale is 2026-27, not 2027-28. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Central accepts TOEFL, IELTS Academic or DET; minimum TOEFL79/120 or4/6, IELTS6.5, DET115. Math gives
stronger guidance: IELTS7.5 or DET135 (145 preferred). Its TOEFL numbers 21.5 and23 are not clearly
identified by scale and are inconsistent with ordinary total-score presentation; clarify rather than treating these
as usable thresholds. Official scores required before an offer; ITP and IELTS General Training not accepted. [s1]
[s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Central rule exempts applicants possessing a bachelor’s degree from a US institution. A completed UChicago
degree qualifies. Wording does not expressly resolve an expected degree still in progress at application time;
ask giatest@austin.utexas.edu if not yet conferred. A US master’s alone is insufficient. Teaching assistant
English certification is separate. [s3] [s6] [s15]
GRE General [2027 confirmed]
Requirement waived effective Fall 2027 by August 2026 update. No explicit not-considered rule found; optional
acceptance of General scores should be checked in portal. Older prose comparing General and Math weights is
not a current requirement. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Optional but highly recommended; no score cutoff, used as one holistic information point rather than a
research measure. ETS code6882; valid five years. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, through UT’s online recommendation system. Public Mathematics page does not establish a higher
maximum or exact referee-question text. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
All admits are considered for recruitment fellowships; no separate initial fellowship reference identified. Later
Continuing Fellowship nominations use adviser support and departmental nomination rather than an incoming
extra letter. Exact nomination questionnaire not public. [s5]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Central page says emails are sent after recommenders are listed, without exact trigger. Two UT departments
describing the shared OGA/Slate system specify post-submission, and SLHS says 1-2 business days after
submission AND fee payment. This is cross-department system evidence, not Math-specific confirmation; do
not assume entering details immediately invites. [s2] [s8] [s9]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Shared-system guidance indicates requests follow submission (and fee payment/processing). Submit/pay early
to give referees usable links before December 15. Verify current Mathematics portal trigger. [s8] [s9] [s1]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
MyStatus tracks supporting-material receipt. Shared OGA workflow displays referee name, sent date and
received date. [s2] [s8]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
MyStatus can resend requests, change blocked email addresses, add a recommender and change retained
access to waived. Replacement of an already submitted letter and reuse across cycles are not publicly
documented; ask gradref@austin.utexas.edu. Do not email letters directly to that help address. [s2] [s15]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required uploaded resume/CV, including publications, awards, honors and notable achievements. May upload
through MyStatus after initial application. No CV-specific page limit or font/margin/file rule established publicly.
[s1]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required narrative, typically2-3pages (guidance, not stated hard maximum), uploaded through MyStatus.
Prompt paraphrase: mathematical/research experience, interests and UT faculty fit,
leadership/teaching/community impact, career aims, personality/life experience and special circumstances. No
spacing/font/margin/file-format rule established publicly. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Separate diversity/background statement not required. Such material is encouraged within SOP; an optional
separate diversity statement may be uploaded as a miscellaneous document. No separate prompt, limit or
format prescribed publicly. [s1]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Discuss in SOP and choose primary, optional secondary and up to three specific interest areas in application.
No separate research-interest essay required in public list; no additional limit established. [s1]

Research proposal [Unresolved]
Separate research proposal not listed as required. Miscellaneous scholarly materials are encouraged, but no
proposal-specific prompt/limit is provided; confirm before treating a detailed proposal as expected. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Optional but strongly encouraged: copies of relevant publications/preprints, REU reports,
undergraduate/master’s thesis or mathematical exposition. Upload each as a miscellaneous document; a mere
link is not the stated submission method. Public page gives no page-count, file-size or formatting limit. [s1]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Include publications on CV; full relevant papers/preprints strongly encouraged as miscellaneous uploads. No
separate publications-list requirement or hard limit published. [s1]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate course list/description requirement found on math or central checklist after targeted search.
Transcript and advanced-course preparation are evaluated. Any portal-only course-list prompt/length/file rule
is unverified; do not infer an additional mandatory attachment. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate initial standard-funding or recruitment-fellowship essay found. If requesting admission without
departmental funding, required explanatory miscellaneous document should identify anticipated external
source and amount; proof may be requested, and do not then expect departmental support. [s1] [s5]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Optional miscellaneous documents can explain special circumstances or temporarily self-report pending official
English scores (title TOEFL Scores or IELTS Scores). Official English score remains necessary for an offer if not
exempt. Below-minimum GPA explanation can be uploaded as a letter. No public extra short-answer limits
identified. [s1] [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2027-28 math offer amount not verified. 2026-27 CNS TierIII (all CNS PhDs) TA scale: USD3,059.50/month,
USD13,767.75 per long semester; two semesters total USD27,535.50 (calculated9months). Listed three-month
summer rate USD9,178.50 applies when appointed, not a universal summer guarantee. First-year summer
fellowship usually offered; amount not stated. Twenty-hour TA tuition benefit covers9resident credits/long
semester; resident-rate entitlement requires qualifying appointment. Eligible AcademicBlue employees
receive100% own premium support (dependent50%); verify fees and first-year fellowship insurance separately.
[s6] [s10] [s11] [s13]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five years defined as ten fall/spring semesters, subject to satisfactory progress. Sixth year discretionary,
budget-dependent and requested early in year5. First summer usually fellowship-supported; later summers
depend on GRA/fellowship/limited TA availability, not an across-the-board five-year twelve-month guarantee.
[s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students explicitly eligible for individual-faculty NSF grant GRA support and ordinary
admitted-student support. NSF RTG support and NSF GRFP are citizenship/permanent-residence limited; do not
equate these with ordinary GRA eligibility. [s5]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Default fall/spring support is TA unless GRA/fellowship available. Employment requires good standing,
satisfactory progress, GPA>=3.0,9graduate credits/long semester or3summer, and no more than two
X/I/NC/D/F grades combined. International TAs need ITA certification. Fellowship holders generally cannot add

employment without a relevant training exception. Appointments depend on resources and satisfactory
service. [s5] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate admission financial-aid application. Recruitment fellowship consideration automatic. Later TA
onboarding/application and availability schedule required for appointments; incoming students submit
schedule when able, with standing returning-student planning dates mid-July fall/mid-November
spring/mid-April summer. These are not PhD admission deadlines. [s5] [s6]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Individual faculty GRA grants, competitive recruitment/continuing/summer fellowships, departmental
endowments and optional summer teaching. Continuing Fellowship department nominates two students; no
direct application, research progress/adviser backing expected. Only about10% receive summer TA
appointments. Texas Global lists nationality-specific funds such as ConTex for Mexican citizens; eligibility
cannot be inferred without citizenship. [s5] [s3]
Application fee [Standing rule]
International graduate application USD90 nonrefundable; domestic USD65 does not apply solely because
studying at UChicago. Pay via MyStatus after initial application processing, credit card/electronic check. [s2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central fee waiver is unavailable to international citizens. Domestic first-time graduate applicants with financial
need submit documentation after receiving EID; an F-1 student should budget USD90. No Mathematics-specific
international exception found. Fee must be paid/waived before document uploads. [s2] [s1]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Accredited US bachelor’s degree or equivalent, adequate mathematical preparation and normally GPA at least
3.0 in upper-division and any graduate work. Below-minimum applicants may apply with an explanatory letter.
UChicago math bachelor is an eligible degree route if completed in time; GPA/history remain unverified. Only
fall PhD admission; mathematics master’s is actuarial only. [s4] [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply early enough for multi-step processing: initial form takes 2-3 business days to load; then pay fee and
complete MyStatus documents. Transcript verification takes another 2-3 business days. Use assigned UT EID,
never create a duplicate. Choose primary interest ANG for algebra/number theory/geometry, optional
secondary and up to three specific areas; choices guide reviewers but do not bind your eventual specialty. [s2]
[s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
List faculty of interest in SOP; no prior supervisor approval requirement appears in math instructions. For
academic admissions questions, Graduate Advisor Tim Perutz: gradadv@math.utexas.edu; program
administrator Robyn Lynch: robyn.lynch@austin.utexas.edu. Individual faculty availability remains to be
confirmed. [s1] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Initial Slate form followed by MyStatus/EID email, fee payment and verified documents. Central processing
estimate2-3business days is more conservative than math24-48hours. Monitor MyStatus; upload scans of
official transcripts, not unofficial placeholders. Referee reminders/updates supported. For international
insurance, benefits-eligible appointment waiver must be processed by 10thclass day5p.m. fall/spring
or1stclass day5p.m. summer; exact Fall2027date not yet published. [s2] [s12]

Explicit Fall 2027 application opening and August 2026 GRE update. Deadline year inferred from current
cycle’s December 15; precise time unknown. Pay scale is 2026-27, not 2027-28. [s1] [s6]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Accredited US bachelor’s degree or equivalent, adequate mathematical preparation and normally GPA at least
3.0 in upper-division and any graduate work. Below-minimum applicants may apply with an explanatory letter.
UChicago math bachelor is an eligible degree route if completed in time; GPA/history remain unverified. Only
fall PhD admission; mathematics master’s is actuarial only. [s4] [s1]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply early enough for multi-step processing: initial form takes 2-3 business days to load; then pay fee and
complete MyStatus documents. Transcript verification takes another 2-3 business days. Use assigned UT EID,
never create a duplicate. Choose primary interest ANG for algebra/number theory/geometry, optional
secondary and up to three specific areas; choices guide reviewers but do not bind your eventual specialty. [s2]
[s1]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
List faculty of interest in SOP; no prior supervisor approval requirement appears in math instructions. For
academic admissions questions, Graduate Advisor Tim Perutz: gradadv@math.utexas.edu; program
administrator Robyn Lynch: robyn.lynch@austin.utexas.edu. Individual faculty availability remains to be
confirmed. [s1] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Initial Slate form followed by MyStatus/EID email, fee payment and verified documents. Central processing
estimate2-3business days is more conservative than math24-48hours. Monitor MyStatus; upload scans of
official transcripts, not unofficial placeholders. Referee reminders/updates supported. For international
insurance, benefits-eligible appointment waiver must be processed by 10thclass day5p.m. fall/spring
or1stclass day5p.m. summer; exact Fall2027date not yet published. [s2] [s12]

English requirement [Conflict]
Central accepts TOEFL, IELTS Academic or DET; minimum TOEFL79/120 or4/6, IELTS6.5, DET115. Math gives
stronger guidance: IELTS7.5 or DET135 (145 preferred). Its TOEFL numbers 21.5 and23 are not clearly

as usable thresholds. Official scores required before an offer; ITP and IELTS General Training not accepted. [s1]

UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Central rule exempts applicants possessing a bachelor’s degree from a US institution. A completed UChicago
degree qualifies. Wording does not expressly resolve an expected degree still in progress at application time;
ask giatest@austin.utexas.edu if not yet conferred. A US master’s alone is insufficient. Teaching assistant
English certification is separate. [s3] [s6] [s15]
